To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the inoculum used in our reinfection experiments contained multiple variants and that (2) the newly emerged variants in the challenged animals were either identical to the challenge inoculum or closely resembled them.

the quasispecies present at the time of challenge are responsible for reinfection, and that the quasispeices present in the inoculum can be out-competed by the quasispecies already present in the host.

the chimpanzee model is useful for evaluating the immunologic response of the host to hepatitis C virus ( HCV ) infection and that the presence of minor HCV quasispecies in chronically infected chimpanzee may be responsible for reinfection with the original infective agent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the quasispecies in chronic hepatitis C virus infection in chimpanzees.
the evolution and transmission of the hepatitis C virus (hcv), a major cause of chronic hepatitis.
the role of minor quasispices in the pathogenesis and reinfection of chronic HCV infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reinfection of chimpanzees with HCV is possible but not inevitable and that it may reflect the emergence and persistence of minor quasispecific strains.

the chimpanzee is a very useful model for the study of HCV infection and that the results from this study are consistent with the hypothesis that the quasispecies present in a challenge inoculum can be responsible for the signs of reinfection in chronically infected chimpanzee.
the chimpanzees were able to mount some immunity to the challenge strain, but that this was not sufficient to prevent reinfection with the challenge virus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCV is a virus with high genetic variability and that the immune response to HCV in chimpanzees is not sufficient to clear infection.
chimpanzee models of HCV are useful in studying the pathogenesis of HCV and the development of new therapies, but the models have limitations.
HCV quasispecies are highly diverse, and that this is an important feature of HCV pathogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the virus is very dynamic.
the chimpanzee is a very valuable animal for studying hepatitis C virus.
the chimpanzee is a good animal model for chronic HCV infection and that it is important to understand the quasispecies structure of the virus in the animal model.
